status: PROPOSAL - research data only. This file is NOT authoritative simulation state and NOT renderer presentation data. It does not finalise a runtime schema. Canonical settlement/location identities (RFC 4122 UUIDv5, ADR-0009) are minted only by the atlas pipeline at integration time; the proposedId values here are research handles, not canonical IDs.
subject: R-16 historical settlement roster, third batch (batch 3) - completion of envelope region 7 (Greece, the Aegean & Crete) and region 8 (Anatolia & the Black Sea)
envelopeRegions: 7 - Greece, the Aegean & Crete (mid ~92); 8 - Anatolia & the Black Sea (mid ~80)
batchScope: Macedonia, Thrace, Thessaly, central Greece, Attica, Euboea, the Peloponnese, Aetolia/Acarnania, Epirus, Crete and the Cyclades (region 7); Ionia, Aeolis, the Troad, Mysia/Propontis, Lydia, Caria, Lycia, Pamphylia, Bithynia, Pontus, Phrygia, Galatia, Paphlagonia and Cappadocia (region 8). Completes the mid targets left open by batch 2.
coordinateConvention: WGS84 decimal degrees, approximate representative points for the ancient site (not the modern town unless noted). Precision does not imply archaeological accuracy and is not a surveyed building location.
idScheme: proposedId = r16-gre-<slug> for Greece/Aegean/Crete (envelope region 7) or r16-ana-<slug> for Anatolia/Black Sea (envelope region 8); the slug (key) is region-scoped to avoid homonyms. Stable, human-readable, non-canonical.
methodNote: Records are compiled from independent evidence (primary literary/administrative sources, archaeology and the Pleiades gazetteer for coordinates). Game/mod faction names are discovery leads only and never authorities. Every coordinate is a representative point with an explicit location confidence; where only a broad location is known the coordinate is coarse. Political authority is recorded only where supported; otherwise it is left unclaimed and listed in unresolved[].
sourceAuditNote: Pleiades gazetteer identifiers are recorded only as 'to be confirmed', never asserted: automated access to pleiades.stoa.org was blocked by the site's anti-scraping protection during this pass, so no Pleiades id has been verified. Coordinates are approximate representative points, not surveyed locations. The Hellenistic literary sources (Polybius, Livy, Diodorus, Pausanias, Strabo, Plutarch, Justin, Arrian, Xenophon for background) are later than 278 BCE and are dated in each record. The 278 horizon is one of acute political flux (the Gallic invasion, the collapse of Lysimachus' kingdom, Antigonus Gonatas not yet king, Pyrrhus in the west, the first Gallic crossing into Anatolia); later political control must NOT be retrojected. Many Anatolian interior sites are attested chiefly by Strabo and later inscriptions, so their 278 political status is left uncertain. Confirming Pleiades ids and coordinates manually remains an integration prerequisite.
politicalContext278Bce: The Gallic (Galatian) invasion is in progress (Delphi 279; Lysimachia 277; the crossing into Anatolia 278/277). Macedon is in chaos: Ptolemy Keraunos killed 279, Antigonus Gonatas not yet recognised king (king 276/275 after his 277 victory). Byzantium and the N. Aegean are pressured. Aetolia is strong and holds Delphi. The Achaean League was only just revived (c.281/280) by four cities. Athens is free but its Piraeus is garrisoned. In Anatolia the Seleucid Antiochus I holds the interior, Philetaerus rules Pergamon as a Seleucid-nominal dynast, Ptolemy II holds or influences coastal bases, Bithynia is under Zipoetes (d.278), and the Galatians are crossing into Anatolia (278/277).
duplicateGuard: None of these records reproduce the 23 active atlas sites, the 12 deferred atlas candidates, the excluded site (Cosa), the 55 batch-1 central-Mediterranean records, or the 56 batch-2 region-7/region-8 records. The proposedId values are checked distinct from the batch-2 gre/ana ids listed in that file and from r16-ita-.
